question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Six months from the date the employee was offered employment in the Institute. [621/2025 §33(2)(b)]

- This applies to National Building Research Organisation officers/employees who wish to opt out of employment in the new Institute. [621/2025 §33(2)(a)–(b)]
- The evidence is the Gazette version dated 2025-07-17. [621/2025 §33]

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Yes — the exclusion applies where the amount was deducted under section 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act "for any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018" [022/2026 §37]. This is the new section 202(2A) of the principal enactment, which states subsection (2) "shall not apply" to such deductions, even if an un-deducted balance remains as at April 1, 2018 [022/2026 §37].

- Same exclusion applies to notional tax credit claims, or any other tax credit under the repealed Act, for years of assessment commencing on or after April 1, 2018 [022/2026 §37].
- Also excluded: application of any tax rate or exemption under the repealed Act for years of assessment commencing on or after April 1, 2018 [022/2026 §37].

Caveats: Section 37 does not appear in the commencement Table in §1, so it would commence on the date the Bill becomes an Act [022/2026 §1(2)]; the text given is the Bill version (2026-03-17), not a Gazette version.

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
A moneylender’s licence issued or renewed under the Bill is valid for **one year**. [653/2025 §25(c)]

- This applies to licences issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24. [653/2025 §25]
- By contrast, a microfinance institution licence is issued for **three years**. [653/2025 §32(7)]

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
At least **thirty days** before the licence expires — the renewal application must be submitted "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration" [657/2025 §6(1)].

- It must be in the prescribed Form with the prescribed renewal fee [657/2025 §6(1)].
- Renewal is then granted if the licensee has not breached the licence terms, not contravened the Act or regulations, and continuation won't adversely affect the public [657/2025 §6(2)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette-published version (GS, 2025-12-12) of the Licensing of Container Depot Operators bill; no presented Bill version is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
The amendment raises the overall maximum period a Freezing Order may remain in effect to **three years**, with each High Court order capped at **four months**; the initial police-issued order runs for **fourteen working days**. [033/2026 §9]; [020/2026 §8]

- High Court order: “shall not exceed four months” and overall “a period of three years” [033/2026 §9]
- Police order: “for a period of fourteen working days” [020/2026 §8]
- The GS 020/2026 and Bill 033/2026 clauses are identical here.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
The levy is calculated **monthly**, on the value of telecommunication services received “in respect of each month” [028/2026 §2].

- Section 2 is substituted to charge the levy on “the value of the supply of telecommunication services … on the receipt of such telecommunication services in respect of each month” [028/2026 §2].
- The same clause text is also in Bill 035/2026 (2026-05-06); the GS version is 028/2026 (2026-04-23) [028/2026 §2].

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
The amended section 49(5) permits notice of dishonour to be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" which sufficiently identify the bill and intimate dishonour by non-acceptance or non-payment [601/2025 §8].

- The electronic route is conditional: the means must "sufficiently identify the bill" and state that it has been dishonoured [601/2025 §8].
- The identical text appears in 612/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-17) and in the earlier 527/2024 and 552/2024 versions [601/2025 §8].

Caveats: I rely on 601/2025's §8 text, which the evidence states is identical across those bills; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
Under [607/2025 §11(4)], a "qualified auditor" is either an individual member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or another Institute established by law) holding "a certified to practice as Accountant" issued by that Institute's Council, or a firm of accountants whose resident partners each hold such membership and certificate.

- The audit itself is done by "a qualified auditor appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [607/2025 §11(3)].
- The financial year is the calendar year [607/2025 §11(1)].

Caveats: This evidence is the GS version (published 2025-06-19) only; no presented Bill version is given, and the drafting in §11(4)(a) is garbled in the text as supplied.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
“Knowledge sharing activities” are defined as activities designed to facilitate the exchange of ideas, skills and experiences, fostering a culture of learning and collaboration [646/2025 §18].

- The body corporate may organise lectures, seminars, trainings and conferences in Sri Lanka and abroad as such activities, to promote its objects [646/2025 §6(h)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-11-20); the definition’s wording includes “facilitate to exchange” as printed [646/2025 §18].

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Society may take and hold any movable or immovable property vested in it by “purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise,” held for the Act’s purposes and subject to its rules [041/2026 §13].

- It may “sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of” such property [041/2026 §13].
- It may also “purchase, rent construct, renovate and otherwise obtain” lands or buildings and deal with or dispose of them as the Council determines [041/2026 §6(a)].

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
In the 637/2025 GS text (published 2025-10-01), the **President of the Institute** chairs both the Membership Committee and the Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee. [637/2025 §18(2)]

- Each committee must include at least one Council member, and that member is Chairman. [637/2025 §18(2)]
- For the remaining committees, where more than one Council member is appointed, the **Council** appoints one of them as Chairperson. [637/2025 §18(3)]
- If the Chairperson is absent, members present elect one of themselves to preside. [637/2025 §18(5)]

Caveat: the evidence is the GS version; no presented Bill text is provided.

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
For licensees/approvals granted **before** the new section commences, resident and non-resident employees’ employment income is temporarily income-tax exempt; for licensees granted **on or after** commencement, their employment income is taxable. [654/2025 §3]

- Pre-commencement licensees may employ residents or non-residents, remunerated in a designated foreign currency “other than in Sri Lanka Rupees.” [654/2025 §3]
- For “a period of three years” from the month after commencement, resident employees’ employment income is “exempt from income tax” and deemed a permissible credit to a personal foreign currency account; non-residents’ employment income is also exempt, with no Sri Lanka income tax on foreign-source income. [654/2025 §3]
- For licensees granted on/after commencement, “employment income … shall be liable to income tax.” [654/2025 §3]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The amendment removes container operators from the long title: §2 substitutes the words "freight forwArders, non-VesseL operAting common cArriers, And contAiner operAtors" with "freight forwArders And non-VesseL operAting common cArriers" [658/2025 §2].

- It is a GS version, dated 2025-12-12, of the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators (Amendment) [658/2025 §1].
- Relatedly, the definition of "container operators" in section 15 of the principal enactment is deleted [658/2025 §3, §4]; pending applications and existing container-operator licences are deemed made/issued under the Licensing of Container Depot Operators Act, No. 2025 [658/2025 §5].

Caveats: Only the GS version is in evidence; no presented Bill version is available for comparison.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
Bill 029/2026 (presented 2026-04-09) amends the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005, both by Schedule substitutions [029/2026 §2] and by rewriting numerous sections.

- Widens extraterritorial jurisdiction over acts "wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka" and removes the need to show funds "were actually used" in an offence [029/2026 §3, §4(1)].
- Adds offences — organising, aiding/abetting, accomplice, contribution, and collecting/providing funds for terrorist training, travel or "foreign terrorist fighter" activity — punishable with a fine "not exceeding one hundred million rupees" [029/2026 §4].
- Extends time limits: "seven days" becomes "fourteen working days", and "three months" becomes "six months" [029/2026 §5(2), §6].
- Introduces special investigation techniques and joint investigation teams [029/2026 §12], plus new definitions including "virtual asset" and "foreign terrorist fighter" [029/2026 §16].

Caveats: the Schedule referred to in §2 is not reproduced in the evidence, so those word substitutions cannot be described.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
Bill **639/2025 (Appropriation Bill, 2025-09-26)** is the newest 2025 bill covering the 2026 budget and borrowing; Bill **632/2025 (2025-09-17)** contains identical §2 text.

- It authorises estimated expenditure of **Rs 4,434,356,468,000** for “January 1, 2026 … December 31, 2026” [639/2025 §2].
- It authorises FY2026 borrowing with an outstanding balance capped at **Rs 3,800 billion**, with loan details in the Final Budget Position Report [639/2025 §2].

Caveats: The bill-level summary is auto-generated; the figures above are from clause text.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — Bill 055/2026 (presented 27 July 2026; the same text was published as GS 043/2026 on 15 June 2026) — incorporates the Foundation as a body corporate [043/2026 §1][043/2026 §2(1)].

- Its objects include contributing to national and social development by developing, promoting and modernising "all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" [043/2026 §3(1)(a)].
- It also covers rural youth vocational training, micro-entrepreneurship, drug-abuse prevention and soil conservation [043/2026 §3(1)(b),(f),(g),(i)].

Caveats: your wording says "economic growth"; the text says "national and social development" [043/2026 §3(1)(a)]. Bill 055/2026's description spells the name "Recourses", while §1 uses "Resources". No penalties are set out [055/2026].

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum is **one year**: the Council may, "in lieu of disenrolling a member," "warn, reprimand or suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" [054/2026 §24].

- The suspension option applies only once the Disciplinary Committee's report establishes "professional misconduct" [054/2026 §24], as determined by inquiry under s.23 [054/2026 §23 §2–3].
- The Council may also re-enroll the person at its discretion [054/2026 §24].

Caveats: The same text appears in 040/2026 and 050/2026; committee-stage amendments are not covered.

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
More than three months. Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, a person qualifies as an “occupant” if they are in “lawful occupation” and have had “undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation” for “a period of more than three months” before the events in sections 3, 4 or 5 [004/2026 §2].

- The threshold is expressly “more than three months,” not exactly three months [004/2026 §2(b)].
- The text says “undisturbed and uninterrupted,” not “peacefully” [004/2026 §2(b)].

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
The evidence I have is Bill **594/2025** ("Gambling Regulatory Authority – GS", Gazette 2025-05-27), not 613/2025 — but its disqualification clause covers this: a person is disqualified from appointment to the Board if "over seventy years of age" [594/2025 §9(i)].

- The disqualification applies to being "appointed as a member of the Board" rather than to continuing in office [594/2025 §9].
- Related tenure cap: appointed members serve three years, with re-appointment for "not more than two further terms" [594/2025 §10].

Caveats: The bill number in your question differs from the evidence; no other age limit appears in this text.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The longest jail term is **one year**, on conviction by a Magistrate.

- For arriving in or leaving Sri Lanka with cash or bearer negotiable instruments above the Minister-specified sum without reporting, the penalty is a fine “not exceeding three times of the value” or imprisonment “not exceeding one year”, or both [030/2026 §31].
- The offence and penalty are in the substituted section 27 of the principal enactment [030/2026 §31].

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
A member who misses the annual subscription deadline owes a late payment fee **equal to twice the annual subscription**, payable by 30 April of the following year [077/2026 §30(4)].

- The subscription itself is due by **31 December** of the preceding year [077/2026 §30(3)].
- If unpaid through the due date plus six months, the member is removed from the Register [077/2026 §30(6)].

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The Act sets no payment date: it only says the body corporate must pay "all debts and liabilities of the Trust existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" [009/2026 §12], with no time limit for settling them.

- Scope is fixed to the day before commencement; debts arising later are not covered by that clause [009/2026 §12].
- Money due *to* the Trust on that same day must likewise be paid to the body corporate [009/2026 §12].

Caveats: The evidence is a Gazette version (GS, 2026-02-05); a presented Bill may differ, and no implementing time limit appears anywhere in this text.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under the Immigration Bill, the offence carries a **fine of not less than Rs. 100,000 and not more than Rs. 500,000** [082/2026 §90(2)].

- The duty is to "notify to an Immigration Officer" the failure of a transit passenger or crew member to continue their journey [082/2026 §90(1)].
- Liability is "jointly and severally" on the master, captain or agent [082/2026 §90(2)].
- This differs from the removal-obligation offence in §89(3), which is Rs. 500,000 to Rs. 1,000,000 per person [082/2026 §89(3)].

Caveats: The text specifies a fine only, with no term of imprisonment stated. Note the cited version is the 2026-10-07 Bill; the same text appears in 508/2024, 513/2024 and 071/2026.

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
The Board Chairman holds office for a term of **three years** and is eligible for reappointment [631/2025 §11].

- This appears in the amendment to section 14(2) of the principal enactment: the Chairman “shall hold office for a term of three years” [631/2025 §11].

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The bill substitutes the definition of “Controller” in section 52 of the principal Act with a new definition: “Director-General” means the “Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act” [595/2025 §6].

- All references to “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” in the principal enactment, and in other written laws or documents, are read as references to the “Director-General of the Rubber Development Department” [595/2025 §2].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS) of the Rubber Control (Amendment), dated 2025-05-28; no presented Bill version is in evidence.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
The bill (Personal Data Protection (Amendment), Bill, 2025-05-08) redefines "public authority" to mean "a Ministry, any Department or Provincial Council, local authority, or a Ministry or Department of Provincial Council" [591/2025 §13(2)].

- Expressly excluded: "a public corporation" and "a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007" [591/2025 §13(2)].
- This replaces the definition in section 56 of the principal Act, No. 9 of 2022 [591/2025 §13].

Caveats: Only the amending text is in evidence, so the full consolidated section 56 is not shown; "Ministry or Department of Provincial Council" is quoted as printed.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
The bill redefines "Export Agricultural Crop" as a crop with export potential *plus* local consumption, formally declared by the Minister as a "notified agricultural crop" under section 2 of the principal Act [045/2026 §5].

- Excluded outright: "paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops" [045/2026 §5].
- Also "shall not include any crop identified as a plantation crop" [045/2026 §5].
- This is the Promotion of Export Agriculture (Amendment) — GS, 2026-06-25, amending Act No. 46 of 1992 [045/2026 §2, §5].

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
“Qualified auditor” means either an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or another institute established by law) and holds a certificate to practice as an Accountant issued by that institute’s Council, or a firm whose resident partners each meet that requirement. [608/2025 §10(4)]

- The auditor is appointed by the Auditor General under Article 154 of the Constitution. [608/2025 §10(3)]

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
Under the Proceeds of Crime Bill, with a Magistrate’s judicial authorization an investigation officer may use: controlled delivery; digital surveillance (including interception/recording of digital, voice and video communications); undercover operations (including decoys); laying traps; and forensic extraction of data, information and images from computers, phones, digital storage and other digital equipment [570/2025 §60] (text stated identical in Bill 572/2025).

- Authorization is sought by confidential, ex-parte, in-camera application to the Magistrate’s Court with territorial jurisdiction, or Colombo in specified cases [572/2025 §56].
- The Magistrate considers necessity, justification and proportionality, and may impose conditions [570/2025 §60].
- Progress must be reported to the Magistrate once every 14 days [570/2025 §60].

Caveat: the §60 text is from GS 570/2025; the evidence says it is identical in Bill 572/2025.

bill has no sections or is too long

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, and the Chairperson must be one of them — the quorum is "ﬁve members including the Chairperson" [054/2026 §7(2)]; the same wording appears in the earlier Gazette version [040/2026 §7(2)].

- If the Chairperson is absent, the Vice-Chairperson presides, and if both are absent the members present elect a presiding member — but that does not change the five-member quorum requirement including the Chairperson [054/2026 §7(5)].

Caveats: The Bill passage is headed "Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media" (Bill, 2026-07-22), not exactly "Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka"; the Gazette text of 2026-06-05 is identical on this point, so no Bill/GS difference arises here.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Under the National Transport Commission (Amendment) Bill (2025-05-08), the Commission sets fares by a formula and Gazette Order, then publishes fare lists; operators must display a compliant fare list in each vehicle.

- Commission “shall compute[]” transportation/omnibus fares “in accordance with the formula determined by the Commission from time to time,” adhering to Parliament-approved national fares policy and specified by Gazette Order [592/2025 §19].
- The Commission must publish fare lists on its official website; each provider must prepare its list “in accordance with such lists” and display it “at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle” [592/2025 §19].
- The Commission may inspect compliance; failure is an offence under section 40 [592/2025 §19]. Separately, it may determine the fare formula after “written representations” of stakeholders and revise it periodically [592/2025 §5].

Caveats: The actual formula and fare amounts are not stated in this bill.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
Bill 037/2026 gives the Mass Foundation “perpetual succession” under the name “Mass Foundation” and the power to “sue and be sued” [037/2026 §2(1)].

- It may “have and use a common seal and to alter the same at its pleasure” [037/2026 §2(1)]; the seal may be affixed only in the presence of two Committee members who sign, independently of any witness [037/2026 §15(1)], and is kept in the custody of an office bearer decided by the Committee [037/2026 §15(2)].
- It is “deemed to be a Voluntary Social Service Organization” under Act No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply to management of its affairs [037/2026 §2(2)].

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
For an industrial park, references to the "Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government" in Part III are read as the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (under the Board of Investment Law, No. 4 of 1978) or the Minister assigned the subject of industries under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution, "as the case may be" [053/2026 §10].

- This is a proviso to the new section 57a, which applies Part III *mutatis mutandis* to transfers of industrial estate, industrial park or community based organization undertakings [053/2026 §10].
- For a community based organization, the substituted reference is instead the Minister assigned the subject of community based water supply [053/2026 §10].

Caveats: The text does not say which of the two ministers applies in a given case; it leaves that to "as the case may be."

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under [078/2026 §33], a magistrate with jurisdiction over an approved place of detention must, "without giving any advance notice," visit it "once a month," interview suspects, and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other documents [078/2026 §33(1)].

- If he observes or a suspect alleges torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, he must "forthwith" order examination by a Judicial Medical Officer, with the report submitted to him [078/2026 §33(4)]; if satisfied on reasonable grounds, he must act under section 31 (medical treatment, change of place of detention, IGP investigation) [078/2026 §33(5)].
- If an inspection shows the place does not meet humane-detention requirements, the fact is informed to the Inspector General of Police [078/2026 §34(2)].

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Bill applies to “civil and commercial disputes” mediated under a mediation agreement, by voluntary referral, or by court referral [622/2025 §2].

- Excluded are disputes required to go under the Mediation Boards Act No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act No. 21 of 2003 [622/2025 §2].
- Also excluded are disputes whose settlement requires terms enforceable only by “a decree or order of court,” including the scheduled categories [622/2025 §3].
- The schedule lists marriage dissolution/nullity, persons/estates of unsound mind, minors and wards, guardians/curators/receivers, adoption, births/deaths registration, partition for rights in rem, probate/letters of administration, insolvency, admiralty rights in rem, and fundamental-rights breaches [622/2025 §30].

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
Under the **Samurdhi (Amendment) — GS (2025-06-04)**, the accounts of Samurdhi community-based **banking societies** are to be audited under Article 154 of the Constitution (public-corporation audit provisions) and the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 [600/2025 §3].

- New section 35A applies those provisions to “samurdhi community based banking societies” [600/2025 §3].
- Separate new section 28A applies the same audit framework to community-based **banks**, not societies [600/2025 §2].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version; no presented Bill version is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
Under the newest Companies (Amendment) bill, the company may apply to court within **ten years** of the Amendment’s operation, make the Attorney-General a party, and show cause why it could not comply; the court may permit re-registration and order return of property previously vested in the State [582/2025 §17] (GS, 2025-04-24; identical in 606/2025).

- Former assets “shall vest in and be at the disposal of the State,” but re-registration can trigger an order returning “all property previously vested in the State” [582/2025 §17].
- Third-party rights acquired in good faith from the State are unaffected; the State is not liable where property was destroyed/damaged or possession was not taken [582/2025 §17].

Caveats: The older 541/2024 §15 (GS, 2024-08-06) contains the same mechanism in slightly different wording.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
Under the bill, all offences are "cognizable and non-bailable" under the Bail Act, but the strict bar applies where the value threshold is certified by the Director-General. [051/2026 §17]

- Bail is refused (except in "exceptional circumstances by a High Court") for a suspect/accused of soliciting, accepting or offering a bribe "of not less than one hundred thousand rupees". [051/2026 §17]
- Same bar where the corruption caused the Government a loss, or gained a benefit/favour/advantage for himself or another, "of not less than five hundred thousand rupees", confirmed by the Director-General's certificate. [051/2026 §17]

Caveats: This is the GS version of the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) bill (2026-07-27), amending s.149(1) of Act No. 9 of 2023; presented/amended versions are not in evidence.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Under clause 11, such offences are deemed **not** to be offences "of a political character or an offence connected with a political offence or an offence inspired by political motives" for extradition purposes.

- The deeming applies "notwithstanding anything in the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977" and covers offences in Part B of that Law's Schedule **and** offences under this Act [073/2026 §11].
- It operates "as between the Government of Sri Lanka and any UN Member State", including when affording assistance under clause 12 [073/2026 §11].
- Clause 8 separately amends the Extradition Law Schedule by inserting, immediately before Part B, an item for offences under this Act [073/2026 §8].

Caveats: This is a Gazette (GS) version dated 2026-09-30, not a presented Bill; no time limit or penalty attaches to clause 11.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the amendment to Section 23R(2) in the National Environmental Bill [032/2026 §18], conviction before the Magistrate having jurisdiction carries a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees", plus "a fine of five thousand rupees for each day" the offence continues after conviction.

- This replaces the old range of "not less than rupees ten thousand and not exceeding rupees one hundred thousand" and the old daily amount of "rupees five hundred" [032/2026 §18].
- The provision is part of the Bill version (dated 2026-05-06); the same text appears in 026/2026 [032/2026 §18].

Caveats: Only the amending text is in evidence, not the consolidated section; the bill is titled "National Environmental" (Bill), not "National Environmental Act".

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment sets the penalty for the offence under Section 42 as “a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to an imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year or to both such fine and imprisonment” [611/2025 §13].

- This is from the National Audit (Amendment) — GS, dated 2025-06-23 [611/2025 §13].

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
Under [076/2026 §7(4)] of the Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs Bill (Bill, 2026-09-24), the person "shall be liable to a penalty of two thousand rupees in addition to the registration fee payable under section 5".

- The notice period is fourteen days, extendable by a further fourteen for reasonable cause [076/2026 §7(2)–(3)].
- The local authority "shall take steps to vaccinate and register such dog immediately in the Register of Dogs" [076/2026 §7(4)], which it maintains under [076/2026 §8].

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
Bill 068/2026 adds "methamphetamine" to the Ordinance's list of named narcotics and creates a new manufacturing offence for the other listed drugs. [068/2026 §2]

- The phrase "heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium" becomes "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" in s.54A(1)(a), with the same substitution made in s.54AA(1). [068/2026 §2; 068/2026 §3]
- New s.54A(1)(aa) covers manufacturing any dangerous drug in "Groups A, B, C, D and E in Part I of the Third Schedule" other than those five named drugs — triable by the "High Court without a jury". [068/2026 §2]
- Penalty: fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or imprisonment "not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", or both. [068/2026 §2]
- Separately, cannabis items 26A/26B are inserted into Group B of Part I. [068/2026 §5]

Caveats: Only Bill 068/2026 is in evidence; no Gazette version to compare.

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No. From the date the repealing Act commences, those entitlements cease: residences, monthly allowances, secretarial allowances, official transport and other facilities, and widows' pensions are "no longer be provided with or paid to" [624/2025 §3(a)–(c)].

- The repealed Act is the Presidents' Entitlements Act, No. 4 of 1986, replaced by this repeal Act [624/2025 §2].
- The cut-off covers anything paid or provided "preceding the date of commencement of this Act" [624/2025 §3].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-07-31); no presented "Bill" text is in the evidence, and the commencement date is not specified.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
Under the new section 316a (inserted after s. 316), "voluntarily caus[ing] grievous hurt to a person under eighteen years of age" carries "imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years", plus liability to fine [618/2025 §6]. The text says "voluntarily", not "intentionally".

- Court may also order compensation, fixed after a victim impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses (Act No. 10 of 2023) [618/2025 §6].
- Exception: not applicable "in the case provided for by section 326" [618/2025 §6].
- Text appears in both 618/2025 GS (2025-07-08) and 630/2025 Bill (2025-08-19), stated as identical [618/2025 §6].

Caveats: Clause text is from the GS version; only the bill-level note says the presented Bill matches it, and no committee-stage amendments are covered.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The amendment rewrites Section 5 of the principal enactment so that the existing "sixty million rupees" four-quarter test applies only to periods "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026", and adds a new paragraph (d) setting a "thirty-six million rupees" four-consecutive-quarter figure for periods commencing on or after that date [017/2026 §3].

- Paragraph (c): "on or after January 1, 2024," becomes "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026," and "sixty million rupees." becomes "sixty million rupees; or" [017/2026 §3].
- Paragraph (b) drops the trailing "; or" after "hundred and twenty million rupees" [017/2026 §3].
- New (d): for periods "on or after April 1, 2026", the aggregate turnover for "consecutive four quarters" must not exceed "thirty-six million rupees" [017/2026 §3].

Caveats: This is the GS version (2026-03-03); how the thirty-six million rupee figure operates in practice is not stated in the bill text. Related registration thresholds appear in §2.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment changes the Section 14 threshold from “more than fifty per centum” to “one hundred per centum,” and replaces references to “person” with a company incorporated under the Companies Act [584/2025 §12].

- §14(1): substitutes “more than fifty per centum” with “one hundred per centum” [584/2025 §12].
- §14(2): substitutes “Any person who” with “Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which” [584/2025 §12].
- §14(3): substitutes “a person who” with “a company, which” [584/2025 §12].

Evidence is the Gazette version dated 2025-05-16 [584/2025 §12].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
The bill repeals paragraph (n) of section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87), and in paragraph (p) replaces “trust generally in the form” with “trust in the form” in the definition of “express trust” [086/2026 §2].

- Section 3 is amended as last amended by Act, No. 6 of 2018 [086/2026 §2].
- The wording change drops the word “generally” from the definition [086/2026 §2].

Caveats: The evidence does not reproduce the text of paragraph (n), so what it contained is not shown.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The bill raises one retirement age from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years" and replaces subsection (3)'s companion provision so that "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years" [058/2026 §3(1)–(2)] (Judicature (Amendment), GS, 7 Aug 2026).

- The 63-year figure applies to the class of judges covered by section 6(3) of the principal enactment (Act No. 2 of 1978) — the bill does not name that class [058/2026 §3(1)].
- The new subsection (4) overrides the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355) for "all other Judges and Magistrates" at 62 [058/2026 §3(2)].

Caveats: the bill does not state the previous subsection (4) retirement age, so the change for magistrates cannot be quantified from this text.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
A person may be appointed as Dean of a Faculty for **no more than two terms** [649/2025 §2].

- This is inserted as new subsection (4) to section 49 of the Universities Act [649/2025 §2].

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation) bill, published as Gazette bill **623/2025 (18 July 2025)** and presented as **Bill 628/2025 (6 August 2025)** — same title and, per the evidence, identical clause text. Its short title is "the Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [623/2025].

- It confers on members "perpetual succession under the name and style of the 'Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka'", with power to "sue and be sued" and to "have and use a common seal" [623/2025 §2(1)].
- The body corporate must "uphold the professional standards of the Facilities Management profession" [623/2025 §2(1)].
- Existing debts and liabilities of the Institute pass to the body corporate on commencement [623/2025 §3].

Caveats: The Act number is left blank ("No. of 2025") in the text, and earlier 2024 versions (458/2024 GS, 470/2024 Bill) cover the same subject; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 623/2025 §2

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
The evidence points to the **Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Bill** (Bill, 2025-05-08), intended to be cited as an Act No. of 2025 [596/2025 §1].

- It makes the Foundation’s members a body corporate with perpetual succession under that name [596/2025 §2].
- The Bill’s objects include residential facilities for patients, support for the differently abled and children with special needs, and free meals/accommodation [596/2025 §3].

Caveat: the evidence is a Bill dated 8 May 2025, not proof that it has been enacted.

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The **Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment) Bill, No. 008/2026** (Gazette version, 2026-02-05).

- It amends section 32 of "the principal enactment", substituting paragraph (a) with "Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige." and repealing paragraph (b) [008/2026 §2].
- The Sinhala text prevails over the Tamil in any inconsistency [008/2026 §3].

Caveats: The evidence does not cite Chapter 113 or name the principal enactment; the link to it rests on the bill's title only. No presented (Bill) version or committee amendments appear.

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
It is the **Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation) Act, No. … of 2026**, published in the Gazette on 2026‑04‑08 as bill **[024/2026]** — the GS version, i.e. published before presentation to Parliament.

- §2(1) creates the body corporate with "perpetual succession" under the name "Al‑Hashimi Association", able to "sue and be sued" and to use a common seal [024/2026 §2(1)].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980, which governs management of its affairs [024/2026 §2(2)].
- Its objects are poverty relief, educational help to poor students, youth self‑employment, fund‑raising and establishing a trust for its assets [024/2026 §3(1)].

Caveats: only the GS text is in evidence — no presented Bill version, so any changes on presentation are not shown; the Act number is left blank in §1.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal)** bill, published as a Gazette Supplement on **2026-05-15**, repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 [036/2026 §2].

- It is cited as the “Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act, No. of 2026” [036/2026 §1].
- The evidence is the **GS** version, not the presented Bill [036/2026 §1].

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment)** bill published in the Gazette on **22 May 2025** [589/2025 §1] is the 2025 legislation shown.

- It makes the provisions of the **Provincial Councils Elections Act, No. 2 of 1988** in force on **21 September 2017** operative, notwithstanding amendments made by **Act No. 17 of 2017** [589/2025 §2].
- This operates “with effect from the date of coming into force of this Act,” without prejudice to certain acts done from 22 September 2017 onward [589/2025 §2].

Caveats: Evidence is only the **GS** version; it gives no enacted Act number or coming-into-force date.

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The evidence does not identify any 2025 bill amending a 2016 Act on a workers' financial assistance scheme. The only bill supplied is the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment)** Bill (2025-06-03), which amends a 2005 Act, not a 2016 one.

- It substitutes wording in section 3(1) of the "Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005", fixing a period "ending on March 31, 2025" [603/2025 §2].
- It is deemed operative from April 1, 2025 [603/2025 §1].

Caveats: No bill in this evidence matches a 2016 Act; the relevant bill is missing.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Bill, No. 604/2025** (Bill, 3 June 2025) — it amends section 3 of the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016 [604/2025 §2].

- The same text was first published as Gazette bill **586/2025** (GS, 20 May 2025); the evidence contains identical clause wording in both [586/2025 §2].
- It sets the monthly minimum at "twenty-seven thousand rupees" (daily 1,080) from 1 April to 31 December 2025, rising to 30,000 rupees (daily 1,200) from 1 January 2026 [604/2025 §2].
- Provisions are deemed to have come into operation on 1 April 2025 [604/2025 §1(2)].

Caveats: Bill 537/2024 amended the same Act earlier; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
The 2025 amendment is **Bill 603/2025, Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment)** (presented 2025-06-03), with the identical Gazette version **588/2025** (2025-05-20) — this is the Act amending the *Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005*.

- It substitutes in section 3(1) the words "With effect from August 1, 2005" with "For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025" [588/2025 §2].
- Any inconsistency between the Sinhala and Tamil texts is resolved in favour of Sinhala [588/2025 §3].
- No new powers, duties or penalties are introduced; only the wording of section 3(1) is revised [588/2025].

Caveats: The bill's title refers to a "budgetary relief allowance", not a "special financial assistance allowance" — the evidence contains no bill using that exact name, so confirm this is the law intended.

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
The **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Bill, Bill 001/2026 (dated 2026-01-07)**, which states: "The Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977 is hereby repealed" [001/2026 §2].

- It also stops pensions already being paid to those who qualified under the 1977 law or related provisions of the 1982 and 1990 Acts, from the date the new Act begins [001/2026 bill-level description].
- It was presented by the Minister of Justice and National Integration [001/2026 bill-level description].

Caveats: The repeal provision is quoted from the Bill as presented; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus. Details of the 1982/1990 provisions appear only in an auto-generated summary, not clause text.

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The **Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment)** bill, published as a Gazette bill on **2 October 2025**, sought to amend the **Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988** [640/2025 §1][640/2025 §2].

- It inserts an **18 per centum** rate for years commencing on or after **1 October 2025** [640/2025 §2(1)(c)].
- It substitutes **“United States Dollars one hundred”** for “United States Dollars fifty” in the relevant provision [640/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: The evidence is the **GS** version only; no presented Bill version is included.

warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 640/2025 §2

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
The Land Development (Amendment) Bill, published 22 July 2025, amends the "principal enactment" — presumably the Land Development Ordinance, though the excerpt never names Chapter 464 [625/2025 §1][625/2025 §2].

- It repeals "or upon his or her marriage" in s.48A(2)(c) and subsection 48B(1)(a) [625/2025 §2][625/2025 §3].
- It substitutes "fails without reasonable cause to succeed" for "fails to succeed" in s.68(1) [625/2025 §4].

Caveats: The bill title cited here is "Land Development (Amendment)"; the identification with Chapter 464 rests on that title alone, not on the text.

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The Finance (Amendment) Bill, published as a Bill on 2026-05-06 [034/2026 §1], amends the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018.

- It substitutes text in section 44(1) to exempt "any newly constructed cellular tower" starting commercial operations "on or after January 1, 2026" from the levy "for a period of five years" [034/2026 §2(1)].
- Section 44(2) is made "Subject to the provisions of subsection (1)" [034/2026 §2(2)].

Caveats: Only this bill's text is in evidence; no other 2026 bill amending Act No. 35 is shown.

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) bill, published as a Gazette bill on 2026-06-25 [044/2026 §1].

- It substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20a(3) of Act No. 47 of 1956 [044/2026 §2][044/2026 §3][044/2026 §4].
- The higher amounts do not apply to offences committed before the amendment Act comes into operation [044/2026 §5].

Caveats: only the GS version is in evidence, so no presented "Bill" text is available for comparison; the sections do not state which offences the fines attach to.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The **Online Safety (Repeal)** bill, published as a Gazette bill on **2025-04-08**, proposes to repeal the Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 [578/2025 §2].

- It expressly states: “The Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 is hereby repealed” [578/2025 §2].
- It also repeals regulations made under that Act after its enactment, from the date this Act is enacted [578/2025 §3].

Caveats: The evidence is a GS version, not a presented Bill.

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions) Bill** (Bill, 2025-01-09) addresses this by invalidating the prior nomination papers and requiring fresh election steps.

- It deems nomination papers for the postponed March 9, 2023 elections “of no force and effect” and revokes the relevant notices [566/2025 §2].
- Deposits are to be refunded on production of the receipt [566/2025 §2].
- Fresh nomination notices must be published by the Election Commission “not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act” [566/2025 §3].

Caveats: The bill’s citation says “Act, No. of 2024,” though the bill is dated 2025-01-09 [566/2025 §1].

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) — Bill [650/2025], dated 2025-11-14, which amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008 (itself "as last amended by Act, No. 12 of 2011") [650/2025 §2].

- It substitutes a new section 3 governing identification of projects by the Board of Investment and ex-ante cost-benefit analysis by the Ministry of Finance, with a recommendation "within one month" [650/2025 §3].
- It caps the relevant tax-holiday proviso at "ten years" instead of "twenty-five years" [650/2025 §2].

Caveats: This is the Bill version (not a Gazette publication), and committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
The **UnV Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — [003/2026], published as a Gazette bill ("GS") on 2026-01-09 — constitutes the Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession [003/2026 §2].

- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [003/2026 §2(2)].
- Objects include children's education, drug rehabilitation and farmer/fishermen equipment [003/2026 §3(1)].
- First Committee to be appointed or elected "within one year" of commencement [003/2026 §5(2)(d)].

Caveat: only the GS version (2026-01-09) is in evidence; no presented Bill text is available, and the Ministry named in §11 is left blank in the text.

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
Bill 576/2025, the **Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment)** (Gazette, 28 March 2025), amends the Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979 [576/2025 §2].

- It inserts new sections 144A and 144B after section 144, letting a Magistrate "dispense with the personal attendance in court" of a suspect or accused for detention extensions, bail hearings and similar purposes [576/2025 §2].
- It also inserts sections 273A–273U after section 273, covering evidence given "through contemporaneous audio-visual linkage" [576/2025 §5].
- New Forms 24 and 25 are added to the Second Schedule [576/2025 §6].

Caveats: The same clause text is cited as appearing in 579/2025, but that bill's title is not given in the evidence, so I can't say which bill you mean if two 2025 amendments exist.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
Bill 065/2026, the **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution** (Bill, presented 2026-08-18), preceded by the Gazette version 057/2026 (2026-08-07) [065/2026 §1][057/2026].

- It amends Article 107 (judicial retirement) and Article 137, raising the cap from "not more than nineteen other Judges" to "not more than twenty four other Judges" [057/2026 §3].
- Short title: "This Act may be cited as the Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution" [065/2026 §1].
- Sinhala text prevails over Tamil in case of inconsistency [065/2026 §4].

Caveats: bills 232/2022 (GS) and 246/2022 (Bill) carry the same title but are different, earlier amendments [246/2022][232/2022]; the retirement-age details above come from an auto-generated summary, not clause text.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Rent (Repeal) - Bill** (Bill, 2026-01-20) — note its title and text refer to the **Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972**, not a "Tenancy Act"; no bill in this evidence uses that name.

- Section 2 states simply: "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed." [006/2026 §2]
- It comes into operation on the date the certificate is endorsed under Article 79 ("relevant date") [006/2026 §1]
- Transitional protections for one year from that date, e.g. no ejectment actions and no rent above the "authorised rent" [006/2026 §3(a)–(b)]

Caveats: only this one bill is in evidence; if a differently titled "Tenancy Act" repeal bill exists, it is not shown here.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
The **Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation) Act, No. [ ] of 2026** — bill [011/2026], published in the Gazette (GS) on 2026-02-06.

- §2(1) admits existing members of the Centre as members of a body corporate with "perpetual succession" under the name "Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children", with power to sue and be sued and to use a common seal [011/2026 §2].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Services Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [011/2026 §2].
- Its objects are educational and IT-skills programmes for youth, run "without any distinction based on race, religion, language, caste, gender, political opinion, place of birth" [011/2026 §3].

Caveats: Only the GS version is in evidence; the Act number is left blank in the text, and the name in the title places "Education Centre" where §2 uses "Centre for Education".
